thread:
incident-bot: PagerDuty page triggered: P1 - internal SRV lookup failures in us-west-2a/2b. Symptom: increased 5xx on service-discovery calls, elevated latency for internal auth and routing. Affected: internal clusters in us-west-2, some customer traffic routed through those AZs. Pager: devon-oncall.

lee.sre: acked. I'm on it, grabbing logs and runbook. @ana-eng-platform can you pull up recent consul/etcd leader state + CoreDNS pod status?

ana-eng-platform: pulling now. runbook: https://redwood-internal/runbooks/dns-srv-lookup-failures (link). quick checks:
```
# kubectl -n kube-system get pods -l k8s-app=coredns -o wide
NAME                      READY   STATUS    RESTARTS   AGE   NODE
coredns-5d8f7d5c8-9x2p7   1/1     Running   0          3d    ip-10-0-12-45.usw2a
coredns-5d8f7d5c8-c7h2m   0/1     CrashLoop 5          2h    ip-10-0-21-33.usw2b
coredns-5d8f7d5c8-zm41k   1/1     Running   0          3d    ip-10-0-33-12.usw2c
```

ana-eng-platform: CrashLoop on one pod in us-west-2b. logs show TLS handshake timeouts to consul upstream and repeated "no SRV records" for internal services.

maria-support: customers reporting increased 502/504 on orgs using dedicated clusters in us-west-2a/b. CS queue has ~12 tickets flagged P1. Communicating status to affected accounts.

devon-oncall: I'm SSHing into the node to check kube-proxy + network tables. Quick test: `dig @10.0.0.10 _svc._tcp.internal.svc.cluster.local SRV` from a failing pod returns SERVFAIL intermittently.

lee.sre: possible root causes: CoreDNS upstream connectivity issue, Consul/etcd leader flapping, or kube-proxy conntrack exhaustion after recent peering change. Any recent infra change? pg-deploy-bot, did we push anything to cluster in last hour?

pg-deploy-bot: deploys: no control-plane deploys in last 90m. Noted a scheduled AZ peering rebalance at 00:30 UTC (automated), but no rolling updates.

kendra-sre-lead: plan: 1) isolate AZ impact & reroute customer traffic away from us-west-2b, 2) scale CoreDNS in affected AZ, 3) check Consul leader and force election if partitioned, 4) if pod-level flaps persist, cordon node and drain.

ana-eng-platform: checking consul raft: `consul operator raft list-peers` shows leader in us-west-2c, but two followers in us-west-2a/2b show long election timeouts. logs: `apply failed: transport: connection refused` on follower in us-west-2b.

devon-oncall: conntrack on node ip-10-0-21-33 (usw2b) is at 98% usage. suspect NAT gateway port exhaustion after peering change. Running: `conntrack -S` and `ss -s` now.

lee.sre: immediate mitigation: (A) route internal DNS queries from critical services to us-west-2c endpoints via traffic routing rule, (B) scale CoreDNS replicas in us-west-2b to 4 -> 8 to give padding while we fix node-level network, (C) enable temporary cache ttl bump to reduce SRV lookups. I'll apply A and B now.

ana-eng-platform: applied CoreDNS scale: `kubectl -n kube-system scale deployment coredns --replicas=8 --context=usw2b` -> rollout started.

maria-support: notified affected customers about mitigation (text + engineering contact) — some ok with reroute, others asked for ETA.

devon-oncall: cordoned ip-10-0-21-33 and started drain. observed that kube-proxy iptables has many ephemeral UDP entries; cleared conntrack entries for pods with: `conntrack -D -s <pod-ip>` which temporarily reduced load.

kendra-sre-lead: while we work the node, let's force a Consul leader election to ensure raft health: `consul operator raft remove-peer` not ideal; instead trigger a clean leave on the suspected partitioned follower and allow rejoin. Doing that now.

ana-eng-platform: follower rejoined, raft stabilized. Consul health checks now PASS. CoreDNS logs show upstream connections restored from the scaled pods.

lee.sre: enabling traffic routing: set traffic policy to prefer us-west-2c for internal service-discovery for 15m window. `trafficctl set-route --service=sd --region-preference=usw2c --duration=15m` applied.

maria-support: update: CS confirmed error rate on affected orgs dropping from ~12% to ~1.2% after reroute and node drain. still monitoring. :thumbsup:

devon-oncall: handing off to kendra for night shift. I'm OOF in 20m. Handoff note: node ip-10-0-21-33 drained and reprovision scheduled; Conntrack cause likely NAT port exhaustion after peering rebalance; CoreDNS scaled to 8 in usw2b and traffic reroute to usw2c for 15m.

kendra-sre-lead: taking over. I'll follow up with full RCA run (network peering rebalance + conntrack misconfig) and create follow-up tasks: 1) increase NAT port pool for affected subnets, 2) add conntrack alerting threshold, 3) bake preventive traffic shift into peering rebalance playbook.

pg-deploy-bot: automated postmortem checklist created: https://redwood-internal/incidents/1912345678/postmortem (fill in RCA + timelines).

maria-support: closing customer loop for first wave; will reopen if errors recur.

kendra-sre-lead: final status for now: mitigations applied, traffic normalized, consul & coredns stable. Monitoring will watch for 2h, then we'll transition to follow-up tickets and RCA. Thanks team. :white_check_mark:
